findings.summary: Hard Top-k expert/router selection is an ordinary piecewise/discontinuous switching mechanism. 2026 Sparse-MoE theory formalizes selected-set discontinuity surfaces; hybrid-system saltation theory supplies the general first-order language for perturbation transport across switches, with the caveat that SparkBrain's discrete-time router should use an appropriate piecewise/discrete Jacobian or finite-difference analogue rather than assuming continuous-time saltation exactly.
sources: Tran Huu et al., Geometric and Stochastic Analysis of Discontinuities in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts, arXiv:2606.19036 (2026)
Kong et al., Saltation Matrices: The Essential Tool for Linearizing Hybrid Dynamical Systems, Proceedings of the IEEE 112(6), 2024, DOI 10.1109/JPROC.2024.3440211

findings.summary: Stable recurrent systems can exhibit large finite-horizon transient amplification through non-normal operator geometry. The observed delayed full/no-persistent divergence after top-k turnover therefore has a strong ordinary candidate explanation: boundary jump followed by recurrent transient gain.
sources: Hennequin, Vogels & Gerstner, Non-normal amplification in random balanced neuronal networks, Physical Review E 86, 011909 (2012), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevE.86.011909

findings.summary: Same-start/same-input-multiset but order-dependent final graphs are standard graph-rewriting non-confluence/conflict phenomena. Critical-pair and conflict/dependency analysis provide a direct ordinary reduction for the synthetic structural duplicate/prune path-dependence line before any stronger mechanistic claim.
sources: Campbell & Plump, Confluence up to Garbage in Graph Transformation (2020/2021)
Lambers et al., Granularity of conflicts and dependencies in graph transformation systems: A two-dimensional approach, JLAMP 103 (2019)
